overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the November 15, 2023 notice was not clearly insufficient on its face, since it listed detailed topics under many headings. The letter also reminded the board to list names of appointees in notices and to respond to complaints within 14 business days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice for the board's November 15, 2023 meeting lacked specificity and detail about what would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Where the complaint does not allege that any particular matters were included on the notice with insufficient specificity nor that the Board engaged in discussion on any matters that included only a generic heading, and we find that the notice was not clearly insufficient on its face, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
